title: Crock of Spots
pitch: A glowing crock of two simulated chemicals. The visitor picks feed and kill rates from a small atlas and paints them onto the dish with a brush, so spots, worms and coral grow side by side and fight at their borders. A blacklight toggle swaps daylight pigments for fluorescent ones, a spill button drops a seeded accident into the culture, and every dish freezes into a poster with a shareable seed code.
whyNow: Timeless: reaction-diffusion is the poster-worthy corner of procedural art, and no generative piece has shipped yet. The spatially painted parameter field is the twist that gives a reason to keep turning the knob.

research.summary: The Gray-Scott model has two chemicals on a grid: A is added at a feed rate f and B is removed at a kill rate k, and small changes to f and k give very different patterns (spots, worms, coral, mazes). The map of those patterns over (f,k) was charted by Pearson in 1993 and extended by Munafo, which makes a clickable atlas natural. Explorers exist (one browser tool lets you pick f,k from a map), but none that paint different f,k onto different regions of one dish, which is the new angle. The update step is cheap (explicit Euler, 3x3 Laplacian with weights -1, 0.2, 0.05), so a deterministic CPU worker is enough; seeds that reproduce output exactly are standard practice in generative art platforms.

sources.title: reaction-diffusion tutorial (Karl Sims)
sources.snippet: Describes chemical A fed at a rate and B removed at a rate; small changes to the two numbers give a wide range of results. Typical values near f=0.055, k=0.062, DA=1, DB=0.5.

sources.title: 49 reaction diffusion patterns (GameDev.net)
sources.snippet: A shader write-up of the model producing organic spots, stripes and coral, using a wrapped grid, double buffer and a weighted 3x3 Laplacian.
sources.note: Independent confirmation of pattern variety and of the Laplacian weights

sources.title: Morphe (itch.io page)
sources.snippet: A generator page listing spots, worms, coral and maze-like patterns from the same feed and kill mechanism.
sources.note: Third independent listing of pattern families

sources.title: pearson classes (mrob.com)
sources.snippet: Munafo's page extends Pearson's Greek-letter classification of Gray-Scott patterns; notes Pearson used one starting pattern and missed some types.
sources.note: Parameter-space atlas exists and was extended

sources.title: Exploring complex pattern formation with convolutional neural networks
sources.snippet: A 2021 paper using the same model says pattern classes run from alpha to nu, plus two uniform steady states, following Pearson's 1993 map.
sources.note: Independent confirmation of the Pearson classification

sources.title: How the leopard got its spots: Revisiting Turing's Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis (Springer Nature Communities)
sources.snippet: Turing's 1952 paper proposed that interacting reacting and diffusing chemicals could self-organise into stripes and spots from a uniform start.
sources.note: Historical frame for the about panel

sources.title: The Mathematics of Pattern Formation (Maths Careers)
sources.snippet: Secondary account of Turing's two-morphogen idea and its link to animal coat markings.
sources.note: Second independent source for the Turing frame

sources.title: Using Randomness Correctly (fxhash docs)
sources.snippet: Docs stress that a piece must give identical output for the same input hash.

sources.title: What is Art Blocks Engine? (Art Blocks docs)
sources.snippet: Says a token hash acts as the seed so the same seed gives the same output.
sources.note: Second independent platform agreeing on seed determinism

sources.snippet: Help page for a browser explorer: choose f,k from a pattern map, regrow from a central seed; needs WebGL 2.
sources.note: Prior art and the differentiator (single global f,k)

facts.claim: In the Gray-Scott model chemical A is fed at rate f and chemical B removed at rate k, and small changes to f and k yield a wide range of patterns including spots, worms, coral and mazes (as seen in search results on 2026-10-10).
Pearson's 1993 work mapped Gray-Scott patterns over (f,k) with Greek-letter classes, and Munafo's xmorphia site extended the classification.
Turing's 1952 paper proposed two interacting morphogens that react and diffuse, producing stripes or spots from a uniform start.
A standard discrete update is explicit Euler with a 3x3 Laplacian (centre -1, edge neighbours 0.2, diagonals 0.05) and typical DA=1.0, DB=0.5.
Generative-art platforms treat same seed gives same output as the core rule for seeded pieces.
A browser Gray-Scott explorer exists that picks f,k from a pattern map and needs WebGL 2 (single search snippet, not confirmed).

inspirations: fxhash and Art Blocks seed culture
kombucha pellicles and sourdough crumb as visual language

design.coreLoop: Choose a recipe from the f,k atlas, paint it onto part of the dish, watch it grow for a few seconds, then disturb it (stir, spill, switch brush recipe) and see where regimes collide. Each named regime you coax into existence ticks off a field-guide checklist (second minute); boundary design between regimes and composing a poster worth keeping is the tenth-minute game. Freeze and bottle the dish to a PNG poster plus a seed code.
sophisticationHooks: Spatially varying f,k field painted with a brush, so one dish holds several regimes and fronts between them
Deterministic worker simulation: seed plus a stroke list plus a step count reproduces the exact dish from the URL hash on any device
Field guide of named regimes whose f,k ranges we measure ourselves with node runs and label as our own survey
Daylight and blacklight palettes via a colour ramp over the B concentration, plus poster export with an invented culture-number caption
design.scopeForOneDay: About 900 lines: Float32 CPU worker (about 192 to 256 square, several steps per frame), brush and atlas UI with keyboard-accessible controls, palettes, hash encode and decode, spill events from a seeded PRNG, field guide, poster PNG export, about panel. Cut: WebGL path, audio, animation recording.
risks: Phone performance: drop to a smaller grid and fewer steps per frame on narrow screens, show a pause control

Regime ranges in the field guide are our own measurements, labelled as such; Pearson letter-to-region details are shown only as reported by sources and class counts are left out because sources disagree
The RD Tool prior-art snippet is a single unconfirmed search result, so the page will say as of 2026-10-10 per that source or leave it out
Floating-point determinism across engines: use only add and multiply in Float32, avoid transcendental functions in the step
